keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «모두가 오래된 학교 도서관에 유령이 나온다고 했다(수수께끼)» 와 «무서운 수수께끼의 정체는 배우고 싶었던 한 사람이었다(진짜 정체)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the mystery (everyone said the old school library was haunted) and the answer (the scary mystery was really a man who wanted to learn). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: Everyone said a ghost was in the old school library.
The "ghost" was Mr. Choi practicing his reading at night.

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.

qs.q: Why did Mr. Choi practice reading at night?
qs.qko: 최 할아버지는 왜 밤에 글 읽기를 연습했나요?
opts: He did not want anyone to see him.
The library was closed in the day.
Seojun asked him to come at night.
evs: "So I practice here every night, when nobody can see me."
In the morning, books lay open on the floor.
After that, the library was never "haunted" again.
One evening, he hid behind the desk with a flashlight.
why: 할아버지는 «아무도 못 볼 때 매일 밤 여기서 연습한단다»라고 말했어요. 낮에 도서관이 닫혀 있었다거나 서준이가 부탁했다는 말은 없어요.
He said he practiced every night, «when nobody can see me». Nothing says the library was closed in the day or that Seojun asked him.

qs.q: The story says, "Seojun did not believe in ghosts, so he decided to find out." What does "find out" mean here?
qs.qko: "Seojun did not believe in ghosts, so he decided to find out."라는 문장이 있어요. 여기서 "find out"은 무슨 뜻인가요?
evs: It was not a ghost. It was the old janitor, Mr. Choi!
At night, a strange light moved between the shelves.
At midnight, the light appeared. Then a book fell. Thump!
Seojun smiled. "I can read with you after school."
why: 서준이는 숨어서 지켜본 끝에 «유령이 아니라 최 할아버지였다»는 진실을 알게 되었어요. 그러니 "find out"은 진짜 답을 알아낸다는 뜻이에요.
Seojun watched and learned the truth: «It was not a ghost. It was the old janitor, Mr. Choi!» So "find out" means to learn the true answer.

qs.q: Why were books lying open on the floor in the morning?
qs.qko: 아침마다 왜 책들이 펼쳐진 채 바닥에 놓여 있었나요?
opts: Mr. Choi read there at night, and books fell.
A ghost threw the books around.
The wind blew the books off the shelves.
evs: "So I practice here every night, when nobody can see me."
Everyone said the old school library was haunted.
At midnight, the light appeared. Then a book fell. Thump!
Seojun did not believe in ghosts, so he decided to find out.
why: 최 할아버지는 매일 밤 도서관에서 읽기 연습을 했고, 자정에는 책이 떨어지는 소리도 났어요. 두 문장을 이으면, 바닥의 책은 할아버지가 연습하다 남긴 것이에요.
Mr. Choi practiced reading in the library every night, and at midnight a book fell. Put these two clues together: the books on the floor were left by him.

ends: Seojun and Mr. Choi start a reading club for grown-ups.
서준이와 최 할아버지가 어른들을 위한 책 읽기 모임을 만들어요.
Mr. Choi reads his first whole book to the class.
최 할아버지가 처음으로 책 한 권을 다 읽어 반 친구들에게 들려줘요.

write.src: “It is important to <u>help people who want to learn</u> because <u>everyone can learn at any age</u>.”
write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «중요한 일 + 그 이유» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write an important thing to do and your reason in English.

chips.b: they have helped us a lot
chips.label: kind

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «It is important to» 뒤에는 동사(help, read)를 바로 쓰고, «because» 뒤에는 «누가 + 무엇을» 을 쓰세요.
write.moreEn: One more step: after «It is important to», write a verb (help, read). After «because», write who + what.

img.cover: In a dark old school library at midnight, a ten-year-old Korean boy with short straight black hair, a red-and-white baseball jacket and jeans shines a flashlight from behind a wooden desk and finds an old janitor with white hair, a gray work uniform and gentle wrinkled eyes sitting on the floor between tall bookshelves, holding an open picture book full of big colorful animal pictures and smiling in surprise.

scenes.1: At midnight in the dark school library, a ten-year-old Korean boy with short straight black hair, a red-and-white baseball jacket and jeans hides behind a wooden desk holding a flashlight, his eyes wide, as a small round light moves between the tall bookshelves and a book falls to the floor.
scenes.3: On a sunny afternoon in the school library, a ten-year-old Korean boy with short straight black hair, a red-and-white baseball jacket and jeans and an old janitor with white hair, a gray work uniform and gentle wrinkled eyes sit side by side at a wooden table, looking at a big picture book with only colorful pictures of animals, both smiling warmly.
